reason: Entry 15(a), verified by experiment. black wraps a long assignment RHS in parens only when the wrapped form fits; at 88 it does (85 <= 88) so black wraps, at 60 it does not (85 > 60) so black leaves the line long. Our autoparen IfBreak fires whenever the flat form misses, with no way to ask whether breaking helps. Adding 'string' to optional_parens fixes this case and breaks strings.py@60 in exactly the predicted way -- one divergence traded for another, agreement unchanged at 20/24. Experiment reverted.

Entry 15(b). Both layouts fit at 60 and black picks the other one: it splits the trailing call bracket in preference to splitting the top-level boolean operator, where Wadler/Oppen breaks the outermost group first. This is a preference order over candidate layouts, not a fit question, and the IR has exactly two states per group. One divergence in one language, so it argues for the general conditionalGroup form without yet justifying it.

Documented in DESIGN.md as a known limit: flatten folds the tree it is given, and tree-sitter groups 'a | b & c ^ d << e' differently from CPython's precedence, so the chain splits at the tree's joints rather than at the language's. Meaning is preserved; the split points differ from black's. Fixing it would mean a package overriding the grammar's associativity, which is a different and larger claim than anything in the register today.

Method chains at the dots, named in DESIGN.md as a known limit and the second language to hit entry 11's heterogeneous-chain bullet after CSS. black treats 'a.b().c().d()' as one flat chain breaking at every dot; the chain is left-nested alternating attribute and call nodes, so flatten -- which requires same-type, same-tightness -- cannot collect it, and the grammar supplies no fields it could use instead. JavaScript's stage A reports prettier doing the same thing, which makes this a third sighting.
